answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A newcomer can earn influence gradually through verified contributions, rather than multiplying votes by minting accounts. This makes a Sybil attack costly: the attacker must acquire and risk real capital for every fake identity, while honest agents can treat a long, audited record as a zenith above each relic claim or knoll of disposable accounts.
